<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** DeCo-Attention: Decompose to Compensate for Low-Precision Attention

**abstract/A1：** Self-attention over tens of thousands of tokens dominates the generation time of video diffusion transformers, because its cost grows quadratically with sequence length. The FP4 matrix products of modern GPUs can speed up attention, but the 4-bit rounding of the queries Q and the keys K introduces large errors. We show that the exponential in softmax amplifies the error of their product QK, which therefore dominates the attention error. We propose DeCo-Attention, a co-design of algorithm and system for low-precision attention. DeCo-Attention is training-free and compensates the rounding error of Q and K along a few principal directions found by a per-head eigendecomposition. The lightweight compensation terms are appended to Q and K as extra channels, so the FP4 matrix product corrects its own rounding error while it computes the attention scores. Once the products run in FP4, the softmax bounds the kernel, and we optimize the softmax so that the gain of FP4 computation translates into realized speedup. With QK in FP4, we implement DeCo-Attention with the rest of attention in FP8 on GB300 and VR200 and in FP4 on RTX PRO 6000. On Wan2.2, these kernels run 2.13x, 2.49x, and 2.82x faster than BF16 attention, and the whole generation runs 1.55x, 1.68x, and 1.80x faster. On four video generation models, the FP8 configuration achieves LPIPS comparable to prior 8-bit QK methods, and the fully FP4 configuration lower LPIPS than prior fully 4-bit kernels.

</details>

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Instant LiDAR: Feed-Forward Gaussian Reconstruction for LiDAR Simulation

**abstract/A1：** LiDAR reconstruction supports closed-loop autonomous driving simulation, but hours of per-scene optimization make large asset libraries costly to build and maintain. We present Instant LiDAR, a feed-forward pipeline that reconstructs multiple LiDAR scans as reusable Gaussian assets in minutes without per-scene optimization. LiDAR measurements provide strong geometric priors, but directly initializing Gaussians from them yields poor reconstruction due to nonuniform sampling and a limited field of view. Sparse returns leave surface gaps, while combining scans expands coverage but introduces redundant primitives. To address these challenges, Instant LiDAR combines measurement-anchored Gaussian prediction, sampling-aware Gaussian scales, and multi-frame consolidation. The predictor refines attributes anchored to recorded returns, while the scales adapt spatial support to LiDAR sampling. Multi-frame consolidation merges overlapping predictions into a compact asset spanning the driving log. Compared with NuRec, Instant LiDAR reconstructs scenes approximately 46 times faster on Physical AI (PAI) and 70 times faster on Waymo. It also achieves comparable downstream 3D detection accuracy on Waymo.

</details>

**arXiv ID：** 2611.32144

**作者：** Iman Marivani、David Van Hamme、Jan Aelterman、Wilfried Philips

**arXiv 学科：** cs.CV

[论文页面](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32144v1>) · [PDF](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32144v1>)

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

**优先级：** NONE

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该文提出 CSC-Mamba，将多模态卷积稀疏编码的深度展开与 Vision Mamba 状态空间骨干结合，用于多对比度 MRI 超分辨率重建，并在 IXI 数据上报告 PSNR 提升。

**排除原因：** 属于医学图像超分重建任务，虽涉及多模态融合与展开式先验，但既不研究 VLM 推理中的 latent 状态生成与使用，也未提供可核查的推理决策或证据筛选线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** CSC-Mamba: Bridging multimodal convolutional sparse coding and state space models for multi-contrast MRI super-resolution

**abstract/A1：** Multi-contrast MRI super-resolution accelerates clinical protocols by reconstructing high-resolution (HR) target modalities from low-resolution (LR) inputs, guided by easily acquired reference contrasts. While purely data-driven deep neural networks achieve strong performance via rich representation capacity, they rely on heuristic fusion mechanisms (e.g., naive concatenation or black-box cross-attention) that lack theoretical grounding. Alternatively, model-based deep unfolding networks enforce principled cross-contrast fusion through explicit priors, yet their unrolled steps remain constrained to shallow convolutions, lacking modern deep blocks to capture global context. To bridge this gap, we propose CSC-MAMBA, unifying deep-unfolded multimodal convolutional sparse coding with the Vision Mamba state-space backbone. By fusing common structural priors from the guidance modality via unfolded sparse coding and globally refining contrast-specific representations with a Mamba back- bone, our approach benefits from interpretable, model-guided fusion and long-range spatial context. Experiments on the IXI dataset demonstrate that CSC-MAMBA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in reconstruction quality, achieving up to a 0.62 dB gain in PSNR while remaining computationally efficient.

**内容简述：** 该论文研究像素空间扩散模型的架构改进：重新审视 U-Net 长跳连接的优化作用，提出非对称长跳连接与 adaGLU 解码模块，构建可扩展至 1.6B 的像素扩散 Transformer 并验证图像与文生图生成性能。

**排除原因：** 属于图像生成中的扩散架构与跳连接设计，关注去噪与 FID 而非视觉推理状态；虽涉及多层特征传递，但未触及 LVR 的 latent 状态、证据使用或停止决策，也无具体可迁移线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Let The Pixels Through: Rethinking Long Skip Connections for Scalable Pixel Diffusion

**abstract/A1：** Training pixel diffusion models remains less straightforward, owing to the ad hoc training recipes and architecture designs, along with the sensitivity to hyper-parameter choices. We show that strong denoisers can be built by refining existing pixel-native designs from the literature. Specifically, we revisit the long skip connection in U-Net and find that the optimization benefit commonly attributed to it is not necessary for its denoising benefit. We further find that the conventional linear combination of features from the skip and main backbone is inadequate for regimes of various noise levels. Motivated by these observations, we introduce two core modifications. First, we adopt asymmetric long skips, which propagate fine-grained information from input embeddings to decoder layers. Second, we introduce adaGLU, a SwiGLU-like MLP block, in decoder layers to adaptively filter information from the embeddings before being added to main-branch features. The above designs give a simple pixel diffusion transformer architecture. When trained from scratch, it scales smoothly from small-scale baselines up to 1.6B parameters, achieving 1.62 and 1.70 FID on ImageNet-256 and -512, respectively. Besides, it natively supports multimodal inputs, such as text and images, yielding competitive performance in text-to-image generation. We release our codes at https://github.com/AMAP-ML/PiT

</details>

**arXiv 学科：** cs.LG、cs.DC

**内容简述：** 该论文将联邦学习中多种梯度扰动防御统一为受控动力学框架，并提出仅沿与原始梯度正交方向注入扰动的 NODE 方法，在保持下降方向的同时抵御梯度反演攻击。

**排除原因：** 主题为联邦学习的隐私防御与优化收敛权衡，不涉及视觉推理状态、证据获取或停止决策；正交投影虽可用于扰动分析，但与 LVR 的 latent 状态生成和使用缺少具体联系，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** A Unified Control Framework for Gradient Inversion Defense in Federated Learning

**abstract/A1：** Gradient perturbations are widely recognized as an effective defense against gradient inversion attacks in federated learning, but they are equally known to impair optimization, creating a persistent tension between privacy and utility. In this paper, we show that existing gradient perturbation defenses, despite their different formulations, can be unified under a controlled dynamics framework, providing a cohesive understanding of their optimization behavior and enabling the derivation of universal convergence and safety conditions without relying on case-specific analyses. Leveraging this observation, we propose \`\`Near Orthogonal Gradient Projection (NODE)'', which injects perturbations only along directions orthogonal to the original gradient so that the defended gradient maintains a fixed cosine similarity with the true gradient. By preserving the first-order descent direction, NODE substantially reduces the optimization cost of strong perturbations while maintaining effective protection against gradient inversion attacks. We theoretically establish convergence guarantees under standard optimization assumptions and further show that, under mild conditions on the gradient distribution, NODE remains effective in preventing inversion attacks. Comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and Chest X-ray, together with a variety of gradient inversion attacks, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an improved privacy--utility trade-off over existing defenses across a broad range of training settings.

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation

**abstract/A1：** Solar filaments are cool, dense chromospheric plasma structures held by magnetic field lines above polarity inversion lines. Their destabilization triggers coronal mass ejections and severe space weather hazards. Segmenting individual filaments from ground-based GONG H-alpha observations (2048 x 2048 pixels) is challenging due to low contrast, turbulent fibrils, delicate barb structures, and annotator boundary variance. In this technical report, we describe SolarFilNet-V4, a targeted segmentation framework developed for the MAGFiLO 1.0 benchmark (Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026). Our method couples a lightweight Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions (k=15) and dual-frequency feed-forward blocks (DFFN) to follow extended flux ropes while capturing thin central spines. A shallow full-resolution convolutional branch operating at 1024 x 1024 preserves high-frequency edge details and mitigates transformer downsampling. We train the network using multi-task supervision over masks, centerline spines, barb boundaries, and pixel-contrastive representations. At test time, we apply 8-fold dihedral test-time augmentation (D4), bilinearly upscale predictions to the native 2048 x 2048 grid, and apply an activity-adaptive post-processing routine that calibrates morphological joining parameters for quiet versus active solar disks. On the official benchmark, SolarFilNet-V4 achieves an out-of-fold validation Panoptic Quality of 0.4340 and a Public Leaderboard score of 0.380. The model contains 15.46M parameters and requires 224.34 GFLOPs per forward pass, reducing parameter count by 36.8% compared to standard ResNet-34 U-Net baselines.

**comment/C1：** 4 pages, 1 figure, IEEE format, Technical Report for Kaggle Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026. Source code and model: https://github.com/indraagustian/SolarFilNet-V4-Kaggle2026

**title/T1：** FlashSegmentator: High-Throughput TotalSegmentator Inference without Loss of Accuracy

**abstract/A1：** Purpose: To develop, evaluate, and publicly release FlashSegmentator, an open-source inference pipeline that increases the throughput of TotalSegmentator without retraining or loss of segmentation accuracy. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study used public datasets: 73 CT examinations from the TotalSegmentator test split (median age, 65 years; 37 male, 35 female, one unknown), 30 abdominal CT examinations from the Beyond the Cranial Vault (BTCV) dataset, 512 training-split CT examinations for concurrent-process analysis, and 55 MRI examinations. FlashSegmentator adds static-shape compilation, pipelining, batched sliding-window inference, and GPU postprocessing. Throughput was compared with the reference implementation (including its lower-resolution modes) and FastSegmentator on GH200, A100, and T4 GPUs. Dice agreement was tested with two one-sided tests (margin, +/-0.01). Results: FlashSegmentator processed 3782, 1810, and 270 examinations per hour on the GH200, A100, and T4 (57.7, 33.9, and 6.4 times the reference implementation and 3.20, 2.50, and 1.22 times compiled FastSegmentator). Dice scores were equivalent for all 117 structures on every GPU (mean difference &lt;= 1.2 x 10^-5; P &lt; .001) and at the examination level on BTCV. In contrast, the lower-resolution modes of the reference implementation processed 181 and 213 examinations per hour on the A100 but reduced mean Dice by 0.116 and 0.241. On MRI, throughput increased 94-fold with all 50 structures equivalent. Estimated A100 cloud cost per 10,000 examinations decreased from 997 to 29 US dollars. Conclusion: FlashSegmentator increased the throughput of TotalSegmentator on data center and entry-level GPUs without loss of segmentation accuracy compared with the reference implementation.

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该文是表格数据上联合分类与生成的实证研究，比较能量模型、概率电路、表格基础模型与扩散模型构成的联合模型，并在 29 个分类数据集上按 FLOPs 与真实耗时与「分类器+生成器」分离方案对比。

**排除原因：** 研究内容为表格数据的分类与记录生成及算力预算比较，不涉及多模态推理状态、视觉证据使用或 latent 推理，也未给出可迁移到 LVR 的状态或决策层面线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study

**abstract/A1：** Many applications of machine learning on tabular data need both a classifier and a generator of realistic records. The default is to train two separate models, whereas a single joint model promises both from one set of weights. Several families of tabular deep learning models can be turned into such a joint model, which raises the question of which joint model is preferable at which computational budget. In this empirical study, we introduce and compare joint models based on four state-of-the-art tabular data modeling families (energy-based models, probabilistic circuits, tabular foundation models and tabular diffusion models) against measured FLOPs and wall-clock time, on 29 classification datasets. Methods are evaluated based on two defined aggregate scores that take into account different aspects of prediction and generation. We then also compare these joint models with every pair of a separate classifier and generator at different computational budgets, to see when a joint model may be a defendible choice against the regular practice of keeping a separate classifier and generator. We find that the best joint model is a probabilistic circuit at the smallest budgets and, beyond that, a tabular foundation model that generates column by column using a regressor (TabICL). Compared with pairs of separate models, this study finds a joint model is rarely preferable but often very close to the best pair, without the hassle of training and maintaining two separate models.

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Towards a Multimodal Aesthetic Agent for Photographic Reference Grading

**abstract/A1：** Reference-guided photographic color grading helps users realize their aesthetic intent by selectively drawing on the color and tonal characteristics of a reference photograph. Doing so requires understanding which characteristics users wish to adopt and translating these preferences into controllable edits. However, image-only reference methods align overall appearance without instruction-grounded selection, while pixel-space generative editors typically produce flattened images without editable parameters, limiting subsequent refinement. To address these challenges, we introduce JarvisAura, a multimodal aesthetic agent that formulates photographic color grading as structured decision-making in an editable parameter space. JarvisAura offers three key advantages: (1) an aesthetic agent paradigm that integrates visual attribute perception, strategy-level reasoning, and parameterized execution for interpretable and controllable photographic color grading; (2) a unified reasoning-to-execution pipeline that connects aesthetic planning with backend rendering and editable parameter refinement; and (3) a three-stage training strategy comprising Parameter-Grounded Continual Pre-Training for parameter-appearance grounding, Reference-Grounded Supervised Fine-Tuning for reference-guided reasoning and parameter decisions, and Reference-Aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization for rendered-outcome refinement with multidimensional rewards and dynamic data derivation. On Ref-Bench, JarvisAura achieves the best scores among methods with results across reported automatic metrics and a 74% human-rated task-success rate, exceeding GPT-Image-2.5 by 9 percentage points.

</details>

**abstract/A1：** Immersive scene modeling requires synchronized visual and auditory observations under changing viewpoints and scene conditions. Obtaining such observations and references for controlled scene changes remains challenging. We introduce SynAVID, a synthetic audio-visual immersive dataset comprising eight indoor and outdoor scenes. Each minute-scale episode combines fixed camera arrays and moving trajectories with synchronized, viewpoint-dependent binaural audio. Shared scene dynamics, sound-source events, and observer poses drive visual rendering and geometry-aware acoustic synthesis. We evaluate existing methods for visual reconstruction, binaural audio reconstruction, and audiovisual editing. Mixed-observation configurations generally improve visual reconstruction on fixed and moving test views, while transiently occupied and sparsely observed regions remain challenging. Methods rank differently on spectral, interaural, and perceptual audio metrics. Geometric and instance annotations expose uneven observation support and local Gaussian representations beyond aggregate scores. Paired references assess target edits and surrounding content, while controlled geometry changes produce listener-dependent acoustic responses. The project page is available at https://avery-xu.github.io/synavid-project/.

**abstract/A1：** Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demonstrated significant accuracy across various machine learning tasks. However, these networks suffer from a huge number of parameters and computations, which leads to time-consuming processes. Consequently, parameter pruning approaches have been proposed to compress DNNs and efficiently implement them. The main challenge in pruning is selecting the appropriate parameters for pruning without significantly damaging the accuracy. In this paper, we propose SPRUNN, an algorithmic pruning approach based on the structural proximity criterion for filter pruning in convolutional layers of deep neural networks. Structural Proximity (SP) calculates filter similarity by considering all filters and comparing each one with the others, effectively identifying less important filters for pruning in the convolutional layers. Furthermore, we integrate this approach with fine-grained pruning in Fully Connected(FC)layerstocompresstheDNNsthatinclude both convolutional and FC layers.Toenhancetheaccuracyoftheprunedmodel,weproposealearning rate refinement strategy during the retraining phase. Experimental results demonstrate that SPRUNN achieves significant compression with high accuracy across diverse architectures and datasets.

</details>

We introduce FigmaEval, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design tasks, comprising 84 tasks and 783 screens derived from real-world Figma design files. FigmaEval adopts a constrained-specification, open-solution paradigm, standardizing task requirements and design resources while allowing agents to independently determine layouts, visual hierarchies, component composition, and visual presentation. To assess design quality beyond reference similarity, we develop 22 expert-grounded evaluation rubrics across six dimensions and introduce a human evaluation arena where professional designers compare agent-generated designs through blinded pairwise judgments. Evaluating eleven models under a unified Figma agent setup, we find substantial agreement between rubric-based assessments and human preferences, alongside distinct differences in design practices and quality--efficiency trade-offs. FigmaEval provides a framework for systematically assessing professional UI design capabilities and understanding the strengths and limitations of current AI agents.

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Longitudinal Characterization of Personalized Hydration Dynamics Using a Facial-Video Digital Hydration Biomarker

**abstract/A1：** Background. Hydration is often assessed at a single time point despite continuous changes in body water. A facial-video biomarker has tracked hydration-state transitions, but its longitudinal behavior is unclear. Objective. To assess within-person hydration score changes, individual differences in fluid response, and implications for personal calibration. Methods. Five adults completed water and electrolyte days with an identical 2.0 L fluid schedule, using facial videos every 30 minutes over 12 hours (250 videos). On a separate morning, each completed a 500 mL electrolyte challenge with baseline and four follow-up videos over 2 hours (25 videos). Analyses assessed trajectories, post-drink changes, variability, time at or above score 50, and exploratory effects of starting score and beverage day. Results. The first scan was the day's lowest on 7 of 10 days. Across 50 intakes, the mean post-drink change was +4.0 points, exceeding a shuffled-time comparison (p less than 0.001). For 21 intakes starting below 50, no subsequent score fell; the mean rise was +11.3 points versus +5.7 expected under permutation (p less than 0.001). Intakes starting at 50 or above showed no rise beyond chance. After 500 mL electrolytes, mean change over 2 hours was positive for all five participants, with peak increases of 7.2 to 22.6 points at 30 to 90 minutes. Despite identical fluid schedules, time at or above 50 ranged from 16% to 100%. The electrolyte day showed a greater mean increase from morning baseline than the water day (+7.7 points), although day order was fixed. Conclusion. Facial-video hydration scores showed longitudinal changes associated with drinking and marked individual differences. These exploratory findings support further research on personal calibration and hydration protocols in larger controlled studies.

**title/T1：** FlowVecFont: Scalable Vector Font Generation via Latent Flow Matching

**abstract/A1：** Fonts are natively represented as vector outlines. Many existing studies on vector font generation have relied on specialized generation or refinement mechanisms, bitmap representations, or externally pretrained models to address the challenges of learning vector representations. These approaches often increase system complexity, incur additional computational and implementation costs, and introduce dependencies on external resources. We show that scaling a simple model enables high-quality pure vector font generation without external pretraining. We propose FlowVecFont, a scalable model for vector font generation based on latent flow matching and trained solely on vector outlines. A Transformer-based variational autoencoder maps glyph sequences into fixed-length continuous latent tokens, enabling standard conditional flow matching for vector glyph generation. The model supports conditioning on class labels or reference glyphs, with the latter enabling generalization to unseen characters and fonts. Experiments on 5M glyphs collected across Google Fonts, including non-Latin characters, show that generation quality improves with model scale across conditioning strategies. In a comparison on Latin glyphs, the 800M-parameter FlowVecFont outperforms DeepVecFont-v2 and DesigNet and achieves quality competitive with the pretrained 27B-parameter VecGlypher. We also provide TorchFont, a machine learning library for vector fonts.

**title/T1：** GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM

**abstract/A1：** Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.

</details>

**排除原因：** 该文用分形边界动力学从 24 字节种子程序化导出隐藏层权重，目标是边缘设备上的常数级 Flash 压缩，并在表格基准上评测；虽含有效秩与局部连续性分析，但针对的是被导出的权重场而非视觉推理中的 latent 状态、证据使用或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics

**abstract/A1：** Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. We formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), a procedural weight derivation architecture that replaces hidden-layer matrices with a constant 24-byte coordinate seed Theta = (c\_x, c\_y, ell) in F\_64^3 anchored near the complex quadratic bifurcation boundary dM of f\_c(z) = z^2 + c. We introduce a large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape kernel, four zero-overhead geometric sampling apertures--Cartesian Grid, coprime 3x3 Rule-of-Thirds (Z/9Z), phi-Vogel spiral, and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod--and prove conditional Kolmogorov (K\_Kolm &lt;= 192 + c\_0 bits) and Shannon entropy bounds. Across magnifications zeta in \[10^0, 10^8\], C^1 Fourier and lattice-noise bases collapse to post-standardization rank ~2.25 and SHA-256 PRNG exhibits avalanche discontinuity (rho ~ 0.019, 50.6% micro-step retention), whereas dM uniquely sustains both rank (~10.0) and local continuity (rho in \[0.81, 0.97\], 89.2% retention). Under leak-free 10-fold CV across four zero-scaler-byte non-linear benchmarks, FNS with an INT8 readout surpasses 0-hidden Linear-INT8 by +3.6 to +10.8 pp while delivering 10.7x-129x total Flash reduction (725x-2,773x hidden reduction) relative to converged Float32 MLPs (90.30% Ionosphere in 285 B; 97.22% Optical Digits in 2,598 B; 97.90% PenDigits in 2,598 B; 87.00% Satimage in 1,570 B).

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该论文主张视频基础模型已蕴含比专用运动模型更丰富、更通用的运动先验，并构建统一评测框架，将视频模型与专用人体运动模型的输出统一转为 3D 骨架表示，在纯文本生成、稀疏关键帧重建和视频增强运动模型三种设定下比较运动自然度、语义对齐、动作覆盖与物理合理性。

**排除原因：** 研究焦点是人体运动生成质量与动捕式评测，属视频/动画生成方向，未涉及视觉推理中的内部状态、证据筛选、停止决策或 latent 推理轨迹，也未提供可迁移的状态更新或监督线索，故不入选。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Video Models are Excellent Motion Models

**abstract/A1：** Video foundation models have emerged as powerful generators of dynamic visual content, exhibiting remarkable capabilities in synthesizing complex actions and interactions. We argue that these models have also become excellent motion generators, with motion priors that are richer and more general than those learned by dedicated motion models. Their advantage extends beyond visual realism and is manifested in two important aspects: motion naturalness, including coherent body coordination, physical plausibility, and realistic interactions with objects and the environment; and motion scope, encompassing a much broader range of activities and semantic coherence, particularly uncommon, complex, and compound actions. To investigate this position, we introduce a common evaluation framework that compares video and dedicated motion models through three complementary settings: text-only motion generation, reconstruction of video-generated motion from sparse keyframes, and video-based enrichment of motion-model outputs. By converting all outputs into a shared 3D skeletal representation, we evaluate motion naturalness, semantic alignment, action coverage, physical motion characteristics, and fidelity to motion constraints. Our results suggest that video foundation models can generate more natural and semantically meaningful movements, particularly for complex and compound actions. Moreover, we investigate motion-conditioned generation through loose skeletal control, finding that dedicated motion models do not consistently improve video-generated motion, while video models can enrich skeletal animations using sparse motion guidance. Our findings suggest a shift in the role of specialized motion models, from generating complete animations to guiding and controlling the richer motion capabilities already embedded in video foundation models.

**comment/C1：** 15 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Includes supplementary material

**内容简述：** 提出面向水下图像增强的目标—差异知识蒸馏方法，将视觉语言教师提供的目标外观特征与参考特征残差联合蒸馏到轻量引导网络，并在多尺度增强网络中按“先校正、后细化”的方式融合。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** TDD: Target-Discrepancy Distillation for Underwater Image Enhancement

**abstract/A1：** Underwater degradation changes image appearance and can compromise the semantic cues used to guide enhancement. Identifying scene content alone does not explicitly specify the appearance to recover or the input-dependent changes associated with that target. We propose target-discrepancy knowledge distillation (TDD) for underwater image enhancement, which organizes guidance around these two aspects of the same restoration problem. For each degraded-reference training pair, reference features from an underwater vision-language teacher provide target-appearance supervision, while paired feature residuals describe the observation's discrepancy relative to the same target. Both representations are jointly distilled into a lightweight guidance network that predicts them from the degraded image alone; neither the teacher nor reference images are required at inference. To align their use with their supervisory roles, we introduce progressive knowledge fusion within a multi-scale enhancement network. The estimated discrepancy first conditions spatial feature updates, after which target-appearance guidance refines the updated features and channel interactions consolidate their responses. This correction-before-refinement design lets target-guided refinement build on discrepancy-conditioned features. Experiments on six underwater benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance across full-reference and no-reference metrics. Ablations and feature visualizations analyze the contributions of the knowledge source, joint distillation, and progressive fusion.

**comment/C1：** The main paper is 9 pages (including references) with 10 figures. The supplementary material contains 8 pages and 8 additional figures

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** X-3DComposer: Feed-Forward 3D Scene Composition with Any Assets from Any Views

**abstract/A1：** Composing an editable 3D scene from images requires an asset for each object and a layout that places the assets. 3D generation and CAD retrieval now supply the assets, but layout still lacks a general solution: scene generation methods couple it with generation, and pose estimators handle one object at a time and need true-size CAD models, depth, or iterative refinement. We present X-3DComposer, a feed-forward model that predicts the layout separately from asset generation. Given one or more images of a scene, the object masks, and an asset for each object from any source, it jointly predicts the rotation, translation, and per-axis scale of all objects in a single forward pass of about one second. The key idea is to treat objects as views: renders of the assets are processed together with the scene images by a multi-view geometry model adapted from VGGT-$Ω$, and each object pose follows in closed form from the cameras predicted for its renders. Camera intrinsics, camera poses, and depth are optional inputs. When the meshes produced by five scene generation methods are kept fixed and only their layout is replaced, the layouts of X-3DComposer are more accurate than the native layouts of these methods. Compared with the stand-alone layout model SceneMaker, it reduces the scene-level Chamfer distance by 52% on IndoorMix, our test set from six indoor datasets, and by 28% on 3D-FUTURE.

</details>

**title/T1：** HS-OVSeg: Multi-Granularity Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Heterogeneous Supervision

**abstract/A1：** Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) enables flexible, text-driven mapping of remote sensing (RS) imagery beyond predefined categories. Despite advances in segmentation foundation models, RS-OVSS remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, semantically diverse datasets with accurate pixel-level annotations. Meanwhile, existing RS datasets contain abundant scene- and object-level annotations that offer valuable semantic information but lack precise pixel-wise supervision. To exploit these complementary sources, we propose HS-OVSeg, a unified training framework that integrates heterogeneous scene-, object-, and pixel-level supervision for RS-OVSS. Specifically, we generate pixel-wise pseudo-labels using SAM3, conditioned on scene-level class names and object-level class names with bounding boxes. Combined with ground-truth semantic masks, these pseudo-labels enable joint training across all three annotation granularities through LoRA-based fine-tuning of SAM3. Our unified training spans 20 RS datasets, including 3 scene classification, 4 object detection, and 13 semantic segmentation datasets, with 1,000 images from the 7 classification and detection datasets manually annotated for pixel-level evaluation. HS-OVSeg substantially outperforms existing RS-OVSS models across both the 20 training-source and 5 held-out datasets, demonstrating strong multi-granularity segmentation capabilities under heterogeneous supervision. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

**abstract/A1：** In the realm of generative AI, models such as GANs, MidJourney, DALL-E, and others have been continuously evolving to generate increasingly lifelike images. This rapid advancement has created an urgent need for robust methods to distinguish between real and AI-generated images. This paper proposes a novel approach for the detection of synthetic images by employing deep learning techniques for feature analysis. The proposed architecture classifies images by identifying variations that generative models struggle to replicate, particularly fine-grained textures and complex object features. Deformations in complexes are examined with the help of the CBAM architecture along with ResNet50. We have performed a selective patch-based analysis using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) scoring, extracting the regions with the most and least complexity for further processing with an SRM Module and ResNet50 module. Experimental results show that our approach achieves high accuracy in classifying real-world images from synthetic ones, contributing to the development of more reliable detection frameworks.

**内容简述：** 该论文研究算法追索（algorithmic recourse）中稳健性与公平性的冲突，提出通过模型多重性（model multiplicity）让系统方与个体分担有效性负担，从而在放松稳健性要求的同时维持推荐有效。

**排除原因：** 论文关注表格决策场景下个体追索推荐的公平性与模型更新，不涉及视觉或多模态推理中的内部状态、证据获取或生成机制；「模型多重性」与多 latent 假设仅为词面相似，缺少可核查的具体方法线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Beyond Robust Algorithmic Recourse: Sharing the Burden of Validity through Model Multiplicity

**abstract/A1：** Algorithmic recourse provides actionable recommendations that enable individuals to achieve favourable outcomes. Implementing recourse for individuals requires significant time and effort, thus emphasizing robust recourse: recommendations that remain valid even under future model updates. While robustness preserves validity, we show it introduces systematic harms by constraining feasible recommendations to regions that disproportionately reflect majority behavior, reducing individual flexibility and amplifying disparities. Thus, non-robust recourse risks invalidation, whereas robust recourse creates a preference for high-density regions in the data that induces unfairness. However, this trade-off is driven by an implicit assumption that individuals alone should bear the burden of validity. We challenge this narrative and show that strategic model selection can help maintain validity while relaxing robustness requirements for individuals. By leveraging multiplicity, the existence of equally good yet competing models, system owners can share this burden with individuals, thus resolving the tension between validity and unfairness.

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation

**abstract/A1：** Real-world generative problems in biology, medical imaging, or robotics, rarely come with perfectly paired source and target distributions. While unbalanced Optimal Transport (uOT) provides a robust framework to bridge unpaired datasets via minimum-length paths in probability space, existing formulations based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geometry introduce a structural bias toward high density regions, often triggering mode collapse. We introduce Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), a novel uOT formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth to eliminate structural bias. This allows CuOT to adapt sampling steps to the local data structure, naturally reducing step sizes in high-density regions to prevent overshooting and ensuring stable convergence. The result is a stable, scalable path-length minimization solver that consistently outperforms WFR-based methods on biological dynamics reconstruction, unpaired image-to-image translation, and video generation.

**comment/C1：** 50 pages, 20 figures; accepted for poster presentation at NeurIPS 2026

</details>

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Sol$^{3}$: Accelerating Video Diffusion for Free via Hierarchical Sparse Attention Routing

**abstract/A1：** Sol-Attn (Sparsifying online attention) combines sparse exact computation with low-cost representative approximation to accelerate training-free inference in diffusion video models. However, intra-block attention can focus on only a few tokens. While preserving these key interactions exactly, the block-level decision incurs the cost of evaluating many low-response members. We propose Sol$^{3}$, a training-free hierarchical sparse attention method that further refines how exact computations are allocated. First, we introduce Gaussian-guided hierarchical routing, which determines the scope of exact computation step by step, from blocks to tokens, using statistical thresholds at each level. Only a subset of members within Mixed blocks that require refinement is selected for exact computation, while representative terms approximate the remaining members. We further design heterogeneous routing statistics that combine block-center correlations with variations in Key and Value within blocks to identify blocks that are difficult to approximate. Among these Mixed blocks, we uniformly compare raw token relevance to select members requiring exact computation. Experiments on video generation, audio-video co-generation, and world simulation tasks demonstrate that Sol$^{3}$ achieves 86% attention sparsity and delivers a $3.07\\times$ attention speedup while preserving quality. Our code is available at https://github.com/FofGofx/sol3.

</details>

**排除原因：** 研究主题为图异常检测中的重采样与评测偏差，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据使用与 latent 生成，其关于调参与无标签基线的建议属一般评测规范，缺少可直接核查的 LVR 方法线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** On the Effectiveness of Resampling for Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection

**abstract/A1：** Class imbalance and scarce anomaly labels motivate oversampling in supervised graph anomaly detection (GAD), but its benefits across detectors and benchmarks remain unclear. In the low-label setting of GADBench, with 20 labelled anomalies and 80 labelled normal nodes, we compare class weighting and up to six oversampling strategies in ten detector configurations from three families: graph neural networks (GNNs), tree ensembles on neighbourhood-aggregated features, and tabular foundation models, on 17 datasets. On the eight datasets with organic anomalies, no strategy has a statistically resolved average gain in any configuration, and which nodes are labelled matters as much as the strategy. On the nine datasets with injected anomalies, Gaussian-noise oversampling (ROSE) gains up to 5.2 AUPRC points in four of the six tree and tabular foundation model configurations, and in all six only on attribute-swap anomalies; in four GNNs its gain is not distinguishable from zero. This gain depends on the injection recipe, which gives swapped nodes an atypical feature norm: it is no longer distinguishable from zero when the swap uses a single random donor or preserves the norm, although most detectors then also stop detecting the swaps. Over the 17 datasets, tuning the tree detectors adds about three points, as much as ROSE, and cuts ROSE's gain by about half or more. With the same source nodes and class weight, sampled graph views are not distinguishable from plain copies of those nodes. We recommend tuning baselines, repeating labelled splits, reporting organic and injected anomalies separately, and checking label-free degree and feature-norm baselines.

</details>

**内容简述：** VenusOCR2.0 是一个 1B 参数文档解析视觉语言识别器，通过多专家共识与视觉验证构建自改进数据引擎，并用并行草稿模块 PTPv2 加速解码。

**title/T1：** VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing

**abstract/A1：** We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert medoid consensus, VLM visual verification, and factorized synthesis supply reliable supervision across pretraining, curated SFT, and RLVR. VenusOCR2.0 couples a dynamic-resolution SigLIP2 encoder and 2x2 spatial token merging with a Qwen3-0.6B decoder, adopting compact atomic OTSL tokens to shorten table sequences and reduce structural errors. To further eliminate the autoregressive decoding bottleneck, we introduce PTPv2, a lightweight ($\\sim$67M) decoupled parallel draft module that combines frozen multi-layer verifier conditioning, a standalone learned mask, and block-causal all-position next-token prediction. On OmniDocBenchv1.6, VenusOCR2.0 achieves an overall score of 96.45 and a state-of-the-art 98.57 formula CDM, substantially outperforming massive general-purpose VLMs such as Gemini-3-Pro (92.91) and Qwen3-VL-235B (89.78). Deployed in vLLM on a single H20 GPU, PTPv2 delivers a 2.96x single-request speedup and up to 2.36x higher batched throughput while guaranteeing lossless, token-for-token equivalence with standard autoregressive decoding.

**arXiv 学科：** cs.LG

[论文页面](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32624v1>) · [PDF](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32624v1>)

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

**优先级：** NONE

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该文提出 HiCal，通过离线校准 HiF4 分层块浮点量化的三层 scale 编码（E6M2 舍入偏置与扩展阈值），在推理时保持固定参数以降低量化 MSE 并提升基准分数。

**排除原因：** 属纯文本 LLM 低位量化的数值编码优化，既不涉及视觉或多模态推理，也没有 latent 状态表示、证据使用或停止决策等可核查线索，排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** HiCal: Offline Calibration for Hierarchical Scale Encoding in Accurate HiF4 Quantization

**abstract/A1：** Block floating-point (BFP) quantization is widely adopted for efficient low-bit large language model (LLM) inference, where the choice of block scales plays a critical role in quantization accuracy. HiFloat4 (HiF4) employs a hierarchical scale encoding scheme consisting of a global E6M2 scale and two levels of binary scale extensions. However, its conventional rounding rule and fixed scale extension thresholds may not fully capture the statistical characteristics of the quantized tensors in practice, leading to suboptimal scale representations. In this work, we propose HiCal, an offline calibration approach that improves HiF4 quantization accuracy by refining the encoding decisions across all three scale levels. Specifically, we introduce a calibrated rounding bias for the Level-1 E6M2 scale and optimize the scale-extension thresholds at Levels 2 and 3 based on the empirical distributions of local group magnitudes. The resulting calibration parameters are determined offline and remain fixed during inference, while the hierarchical encoding continues to adapt to individual blocks through their local values. This design eliminates the need for per-block multi-candidate scale search while preserving the original deterministic HiF4 encoding procedure. Experiments across five synthetic and real activation distributions show that the proposed method reduces quantization MSE by 9.91%-23.50% relative to the original HiF4 scheme, including a 13.00% reduction on real Qwen3-8B activations. End-to-end evaluations across six benchmarks further show average-score improvements of 0.91 and 1.25 percentage points on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, respectively, without per-block multi-candidate search during inference.

</details>

**title/T1：** On the Capabilities and Limitations of Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Cloud Segmentation

**abstract/A1：** Recent advances in vision-language foundation models have enabled open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) without task-specific training, offering new opportunities for Earth Observation (EO) applications. However, their capabilities for cloud detection remain insufficiently explored. In this work, we evaluate twelve OVSS approaches across six publicly available EO datasets in a zero-shot setting, i.e., without fine-tuning or adaptation to the target data. We investigate both binary cloud detection and multiclass segmentation, distinguishing between thick clouds, thin clouds, cloud shadows, and background. Our results show differences in performance across models and datasets, with SegEarth-OV3 achieving the highest binary cloud detection performance on four of the six datasets. While several approaches demonstrate promising performance in binary cloud detection, multiclass segmentation remains more challenging, particularly when distinguishing between fine-grained cloud categories. Furthermore, our controlled prompt sensitivity analysis reveals model-dependent responses to alternative textual descriptions, with appearance-oriented prompts benefiting certain approaches while degrading the performance of others. Overall, our findings demonstrate both the potential and current limitations of zero-shot OVSS for cloud detection, establishing a comparative benchmark for future research on generalisable cloud segmentation. Code will be available at: https://github.com/josesosajs/zero-shot-cloudovss.

**title/T1：** Completion-Aware Compression for Progressive 3D Gaussian Splatting

**abstract/A1：** 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-quality novel-view rendering, but its large scene representations are costly to transmit. Pruning and compression reduce file sizes, yet progressive delivery also requires usable reconstructions before the full scene arrives. Existing progressive representations provide partial scenes, but level-based updates are limited by predefined coding boundaries. This paper presents a progressive 3DGS codec that balances attribute fidelity with the image benefit of making Gaussians available earlier. Its single compact stream supports partial 3D reconstruction and adds newly decoded Gaussians as more bytes arrive. The stream supports fine-grained updates at arbitrary received-byte budgets, without separate encodings or later attribute refinement. At matched complete-file sizes and received bytes, completion-aware allocation improves 1/8 PSNR over attribute-only allocation by 0.48-1.43 dB. The proposed codec compresses original 3DGS representations by 62-88 times while retaining near-reference Full PSNR. Under the evaluated 50-Mbps delivery model, partial reconstruction becomes available in approximately 0.2 s.

**arXiv 学科：** cs.LG

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 提出 LATEC，一种基于 GNN 学习预测器、可跨维度使用的有逐点误差界张量压缩编解码方法，用于高维科学数据存储。

**排除原因：** 该文关注科学数据的有损压缩与误差界，不涉及多模态推理状态、视觉证据筛选或 latent 推理过程，未提供可核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** LATEC: Learned Axial TEnsor Compression for High-Dimensional Scientific Data

**abstract/A1：** With the growing scale of scientific simulation and infrastructure, part of the burden has shifted from producing scientific data to analyzing and storing it. Compression is a key step to expanding storage capacity, but requires dedicated techniques to enforce user-specified pointwise error bounds that ensure the validity of downstream scientific workflows. To further push the limits of compression, novel learned codecs have been developed, in particular for images and videos, but these methods often optimize for aggregated distortion and fail to meet error bound standards. Moreover, these methods often target fixed field dimensionality, failing to account for many scientific data use cases, or at the expense of large adaptation or retraining costs. In this work, we introduce the Learned Axial TEnsor Compression (LATEC) method, an error-bounded codec with a dimension-agnostic learned predictor based on a GNN architecture. LATEC is pretrained on synthetic 2-D and 4-D fields, and evaluated with and without domain fine-tuning on 13 scientific fields in 3-D to 5-D. Results show that LATEC is consistently competitive with SZ3, achieving an 18.1% average improvement and greater consistency across all domains than other compressors. These results demonstrate that a shared learned predictor can serve as a single error-bounded codec across tensor dimensionalities, competitive with specialized compressors, while retaining pointwise error guarantees.

</details>

**作者：** Reda Bensaid、Ismail Ben Ayed、François Leduc-Primeau、Vincent Gripon

**arXiv 学科：** cs.CV

[论文页面](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32672v1>) · [PDF](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32672v1>)

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

**优先级：** NONE

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该文把少样本视觉语言适配重新解释为贝叶斯问题，提出在冻结特征上做凸逻辑回归的 TASP，将类名嵌入作为加权样本与正则先验，并在 11 个数据集基准上取得领先准确率。

**排除原因：** 这是少样本图像分类的适配方法，不涉及推理期 latent 状态、视觉证据筛选或停止决策；「表征质量比适配机制更关键」仅是泛化结论，未提供可供 LVR 核查的具体机制线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Text Is Just Another Shot in Vision-Language Models: Simple Probes on Frozen Encoders Do It

**abstract/A1：** Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models has produced increasingly elaborate methods built on CLIP and on one shared principle: the zero-shot text classifier is the anchor, and labeled images only correct it. We argue that this principle reflects CLIP's visual features rather than a property of the task. We provide a simple Bayesian interpretation, in which a class name is worth exactly kappa = sigma^2 / tau^2 labeled images, the ratio between the visual spread of a class and the misalignment of its name. The Bayes classifier of this model counts text as kappa more samples. With modern frozen encoders, few-shot adaptation then reduces to a well-regularised convex probe. Specifically, we introduce TASP, a simple convex logistic regression on frozen features that incorporates class-name embeddings as weighted training examples and as a regularization prior. On the standard 11-dataset benchmark, TASP with frozen PE-Core-L features achieves 87.1% accuracy at 1 shot and 91.4% at 16 shots, outperforming state-of-the-art few-shot vision-language adaptation methods by 4.6 to 11.0 percentage points. While stronger representations explain much of this improvement, controlled comparisons on matched features show that existing frozen-encoder adaptation methods do not materially improve on this probe. We further find that the weight assigned to text matters more than how it is incorporated, and that combining self-supervised visual features with vision-language representations is most beneficial for weaker visual encoders. Together, these findings suggest that progress in few-shot vision-language adaptation depends more on representation quality and the appropriate use of text supervision than on increasingly complex adaptation mechanisms.

</details>

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** CAPTA: Identifying LLMs Behind AI Agents

**abstract/A1：** Large language model (LLM)-based agents access remote services through tools to complete user tasks, often via API calls. In this setting, a remote service may want to identify the backend LLM of an agent to launch model-specific attacks, including prompt injection or selective delivery of manipulated content. However, the service cannot directly query the backend model and must instead collect observable responses through its interactions with the agent, making identification challenging. In this paper, we present Completely Automated Preference Test to tell LLMs Apart (CAPTA), a model identification approach inspired by CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart), which distinguishes humans from automated programs. CAPTA presents multiple-choice questions as verification challenges, using differences in models' selection preferences to identify the backend LLM. It selects questions based on cross-model option-generation diversity and uses LLM-guided search to optimize their option sets. Our evaluation shows that CAPTA achieves 99.0% mean identification accuracy with only 10 questions across 25 LLMs from 10 model families. We further evaluate CAPTA with four widely used agents and seven representative LLMs, achieving 99.7% mean identification accuracy across all 28 agent-LLM combinations with 30 submitted answers.

</details>

These conditions provide adjacent fine-scale structures and an overview of the scene generated so far. To integrate these complementary cues, we map both forms of history and the target to a shared canvas coordinate system to express their spatial relationships and scale differences. We further introduce a Wavefront-AutoRegressive inference schedule that generates tiles on the same anti-diagonal concurrently across GPUs to reduce single-image latency.

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis &amp; Improved Rates

**abstract/A1：** Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysis is a fine-grained characterization of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics. This sharper control of the trajectory further yields tight convergence guarantees within the stable regime, improving existing bounds even in the deterministic setting. Taken together, our results show that the acceleration mechanism induced by large stepsizes survives stochasticity and extends beyond linear models. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of large learning rates in practice.

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Breaking the Joint Action Space Dependence in Distributionally Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

**abstract/A1：** We study the sample complexity of learning robust coarse correlated equilibria (CCE) in finite-horizon, general-sum, distributionally robust Markov games with known rewards and a generative model of the nominal transitions. Each player evaluates a policy by its worst-case return over total-variation (TV) balls centered at the nominal transition distribution of every stage, state, and joint action; this is the standard $(s,a)$-rectangular uncertainty set. Existing generative-model guarantees for this model scale with the number $\\prod\_iA\_i$ of joint actions, where $A\_i$ is the number of actions of player~$i$. Since this number grows exponentially with the number of players, these guarantees suffer from the curse of multiagency. We design an algorithm whose sample complexity depends on the action sets only through the largest individual action-set size $A\_\*:=\\max\_iA\_i$. The algorithm uses $\\widetilde O(SA\_\*H^5D^4/\\varepsilon^4)$ transition samples and, with probability at least $1-δ$, returns a Markov policy that is an $\\varepsilon$-robust CCE from every initial state. Here $S$ is the number of states, $H$ is the horizon, and $D:=\\max\_i\\min\\{H,1/ρ\_i\\}$, where $ρ\_i$ is the TV radius of player~$i$. Two ingredients make this possible: a plug-in estimate of the robust backup whose mean error does not depend on the number of states, and a single batch of samples per round that serves as bandit feedback for all players at once. The result shows that the dependence on $\\prod\_iA\_i$ can be avoided without modifying the $(s,a)$-rectangular uncertainty set.

**comment/C1：** preprint, work in progress

</details>

**abstract/A1：** Ptychography provides high-resolution lensless imaging across X-ray, electron, and optical microscopy, but reconstructing images from diffraction measurements generally requires computationally intensity iterative phase retrieval. These methods often require experiment-specific analysis, limiting real-time feedback as data acquisition rates increase. Here, we demonstrate PtychoFM, a physics-aware foundation model for ptychographic imaging that combines large-scale pre-training with experiment-specific fine-tuning to reconstruct complex object images directly from individual diffraction patterns. Trained using a differentiable forward model without object-space labels, PtychoFM transfers from step-scan training data on one sample to fly-scan measurements of other samples with different feature sizes, morphologies, and refraction indices. At a synchrotron beamline, diffraction frames were streamed from the detector to a single GPU for inference at up to 200 frames per second and returned for real-time visualization. PtychoFM provides a practical route to rapid, transferable ptychographic reconstruction and live experimental feedback under nonideal conditions.

**abstract/A1：** Satellite-based 3D reconstruction is limited by sparse observations and changes across acquisition dates. Existing methods use generative priors to recover missing visual detail, but ghosting, streaking, and blur persist in their Gaussian scenes. These artifacts become particularly apparent in low-elevation renderings. We introduce CityRecast to suppress these artifacts through Gaussian scene repair and supervision calibration. To correct the Gaussian distributions that produce these artifacts, we first use multi-angle warm-up to constrain their spatial extent. This reduces the initial ghosting carried into progressive refinement. Surface-guided replacement then continues to repair the Gaussian distribution while preserving existing appearance. To provide more reliable supervision for this process, observation calibration mitigates interference from multi-temporal observations. Joint refinement further reduces conflicts among generated views. Experiments on DFC2019 and IARPA demonstrate reduced artifacts in low-elevation renderings while maintaining satellite-view fidelity. Compared with Skyfall-GS, CityRecast reduces FID-CLIP by 25.3% on DFC2019 and 51.8% on IARPA. MUSIQ increases by 14.54 and 24.95 points, respectively.

**title/T1：** Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers

**abstract/A1：** Training Transformers requires careful hyperparameter tuning, which becomes increasingly costly for large models. We introduce UDV-Rebalance (UDVR), a reparameterization that inserts an auxiliary diagonal matrix $D$ between naturally paired weight matrices $(U,V)$ appearing throughout Transformer architectures. UDVR periodically rebalances the factors to maintain unit-norm columns in $U$ and unit-norm rows in $V$, with $D$ absorbing the corresponding scales. With rebalancing, a single hyperparameter setting of UDVR remains effective across model scales, architectures, and data distributions. This yields a tuning-free rule that adapts to each weight matrix using only its dimensions. We fit this rule once on ViT models trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and it remains valid when the activation function or the optimizer is changed. The same rule transfers to new image domains in DomainNet, to ViT, Swin, and MaxViT on ImageNet, and to language-model pretraining with up to 1.3B parameters. UDVR consistently outperforms Weight Normalization and $σ$Reparam and matches a vanilla baseline whose hyperparameters are swept on each target model.

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions

**abstract/A1：** Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization. By sharing a scale factor across groups of 16 or 32 elements, these formats enable aggressive low-precision quantization with minimal accuracy degradation, particularly when combined with modern PTQ algorithms. Their accuracy depends on how the numerical format interacts with rotation, PTQ, and scale selection. We study the composability of PTQ configurations across six LLMs and three microscaling formats: MXFP6, MXFP4, and NVFP4, systematically varying Hadamard rotation granularity, PTQ algorithm, and scale-selection strategy. Our central finding is that effective quantization recipes are format dependent: both MXFP4 and NVFP4 support accurate 4-bit inference, but techniques that benefit one do not necessarily transfer to the other. MXFP4 benefits substantially from rotation and error-correcting PTQ, whereas NVFP4 gains less from rotation, consistent with its finer-grained scales capturing more within-block variation. Building on these findings, we introduce Midmax, a calibration-free scale-selection strategy that mitigates clipping error in power-of-two block scales and improves accuracy across a majority of the evaluated MXFP4 configurations. We show that pairing MXFP6 activations with MXFP4 weights recovers most of the accuracy lost at 4-bit and, on Llama-3.1-8B, matches or exceeds our in-house BF16 baseline. An additional study finds that augmenting MXFP4 with a per-tensor macroscale, a mechanism intrinsic to NVFP4, does not improve average accuracy, suggesting that global rescaling alone does not address the limitations of E8M0 block scales for MXFP4 quantization. Together, these results provide practical guidance for combining numerical formats, rotation, PTQ, and scale selection for accurate low-precision LLM inference.

</details>

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Simultaneously Boosting Efficiency and Capability for Linear Attention via Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification

**abstract/A1：** Self-attention's quadratic complexity constitutes a core bottleneck for Vision Transformers (ViTs). Existing efficiency-oriented optimizations, including softmax-based and linear attention (LA) variants, generally compromise model representational capacity, leading to inevitable performance degradation. We propose a novel linear attention which alleviates this efficiency-capability dilemma. For the first time, we embed an Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification (ACCAP) mechanism into the QKV projection of linear attention, which enables the model to retain high-dimensional feature information while performing computations with reduced channels. We further fuse a focused kernel function and a self-gating module into ACCAP to construct a lightweight linear attention module (ACCAP-LA). Our theoretical analysis shows that, compared to standard linear attention, ACCAP-LA reduces the attention module's parameter count by 79.17% and FLOPs by 77.5%. Extensive experiments demonstrate ACCAP-LA's effectiveness: when applied to ViT, it achieves 79.4% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with only 5.8M parameters, and more notably, it boasts strong cross-architecture compatibility, boosting EfficientViT-b1 and PVT-T by 3.3% and 3.4% respectively.

**title/T1：** DualSpec: Spectral Reconstruction with Optimized Stereo Cameras

**abstract/A1：** Spectral imaging captures information that ordinary RGB sensors cannot, but dedicated spectral cameras can be expensive and bulky. Recovering dense spectra from RGB images offers an accessible alternative, but distinct spectra can produce the same camera response, generating an ambiguity that even more advanced recovery algorithms cannot always resolve. Therefore, increasing the spectral information captured at acquisition is essential. We propose DualSpec, a stereo acquisition framework that jointly optimizes two external optical filters and a reconstruction network. Each filter is placed in front of a standard RGB camera, and the two are designed to produce six responses that provide complementary information for the network. Experiments across reconstruction architectures and spectral ranges show that DualSpec reduces mean spectral angle error by 36-72% relative to a single RGB camera and by 11-29% relative to stereo pairs selected from commercial filters. Cross-dataset evaluations, including a new benchmark of spectral images captured from displaced viewpoints, show that the method generalizes and remains robust to viewpoint misalignment, while analyses of thin-film approximations support optical feasibility.

**title/T1：** IMPACT-Seg: Consistent Anatomical Segmentation and Representation Learning Across CT, CBCT, and MRI

**abstract/A1：** Computed tomography (CT), cone-beam CT (CBCT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provide complementary representations of the same underlying anatomy, yet substantial differences in image appearance challenge consistent segmentation and deformable registration in adaptive radiotherapy. We investigate whether dense anatomical segmentation supervision can promote cross-modality correspondence without explicit feature alignment. We introduce IMPACT-Seg, which segments 126 structures across CT, CBCT, and MRI using shared network parameters. A collection of 8,290 volumes was assembled from public cohorts through label harmonization, model-assisted pseudo-label completion, iterative refinement, and 2,864 physics-based CBCT simulations with voxel-aligned CT labels. Unpaired images were used to jointly train 2.5D and 3D residual-encoder networks. On 139 real CBCTs, IMPACT-Seg 3D achieved a mean Dice of 0.842 versus 0.671 for the strongest comparator. On 497 voxel-aligned CT-simulated-CBCT pairs, the CT-to-CBCT Dice decrease was 0.022 versus 0.153-0.178 for competing methods. On independent pancreatic radiotherapy CBCTs, gastrointestinal Dice was 0.735 versus 0.634 for TotalSegmentator. Prediction agreement reached 0.881 on registered CT-CBCT and 0.790 on CT-MRI pairs. Adding MRI training data reduced CT-MRI encoder feature retrieval error from 36.8 to 3.2 mm. Registration pipelines incorporating IMPACT-Seg features ranked first on two multimodal Learn2Reg benchmarks. The 3D model segmented a whole-body CT in 15 s. These findings show that dense anatomical segmentation supervision can support consistent anatomical representations across modalities, with applications to both segmentation and registration. Code, datasets, and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/HEMONCedric/IMPACTSeg.

**title/T1：** HARI4D: Hand-Articulation Aware 4D Reconstruction of Human-Object Interaction

**abstract/A1：** Reasoning about human-object interaction from RGB cameras is important for gaming, VR environments, and robot learning. Yet 4D reconstruction from a monocular RGB camera is challenging, especially when articulated hands are involved. Prior full-body works neglect hands during reconstruction, causing them to penetrate into, or float from the object. We present HARI4D, a hand-articulation-aware method for reconstructing spatially and temporally consistent 4D human-object interaction from monocular RGB video. We introduce a history-aware object tracker that provides robust and stable tracking. Based on these tracks, we improve the interaction configuration through coarse-to-fine reasoning that follows the order of object manipulation: ReachNet first brings the full body and arms to the object during contact, and TouchNet then finalizes hand articulation according to temporal context and local object geometry. On ARCTIC, unseen in training, our method reduces the object error by 56% and improves hand contact F1 from 0.866 to 0.921 over prior art. Our method recovers accurate full body-object interaction with coherent hand articulations and applies to online videos. Our code and pretrained models will be released.

To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% of attempts at about one-sixth of GPT-6 Astra's estimated token cost per attempt, while GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%. We also found that harness choice had little effect on either performance or safety with all harnesses scoring between 42.9 (Claude Code) and 45.2 (OpenClaw) for pass@1.

**title/T1：** FedTumor-IoMT: Federated Learning-Aided Brain Tumor Diagnosis on Resource-Constrained Edge IoMT Devices

**abstract/A1：** Joint brain tumor segmentation and classification models are computationally intensive, limiting their training on resource-constrained edge platforms and restricting privacy-preserving Federated Learning FL in the Internet of Medical Things IoMT. Existing approaches either perform both tasks on GPU-equipped workstations or support only classification on edge devices. To address this gap, this work proposes a lightweight multitask FL framework for joint segmentation and classification through local edge training. A shared pretrained LiteMedSAM encoder with TinyViT extracts features for a coordinate-attention-based segmentation decoder and a segmentation-guided classification head, eliminating a separate feature extractor. Selective encoder freezing retains 95\\% trainable parameters while reducing on-device training costs. The proposed framework is experimentally validated on a laboratory testbed of five resource-constrained edge clients using 1,200 T1-weighted MRI samples. It achieves 94.20\\% classification accuracy, 88.53\\% DSC, 83.68\\% IoU, and 99.87\\% ROC-AUC. Its classification accuracy remains within 0.6\\% of the GPU-trained baseline of 95.21\\% across five FL rounds. The attention and feature refinement modules improve DSC and IoU by 3.82\\% and 4.60\\%, respectively, with 0.74 GFLOPs of additional computation. On edge hardware, the framework achieves 46.54 s inference latency, 52.8\\% CPU utilization, and a peak temperature of 65$^\\circ$C without thermal throttling. Its inference latency is observed to be 6.4--10.5 times lower than that of existing frameworks. These results demonstrate the feasibility of privacy-preserving joint brain tumor segmentation and classification on resource-constrained edge platforms.

</details>

**title/T1：** NEST: Uncovering and Nesting Unknown Objects in Open-World Object Detection

**abstract/A1：** Open-world object detectors aim to localize objects of classes not covered by their training annotations, but most label them only as "unknown". This label tells a system that an object is present but not what it is, while its broader category would allow a more informed decision. We therefore address both uncovering unknown objects and assigning them to the broader categories of a given class taxonomy. For uncovering, we find that most unknown objects are already localized and labeled "unknown" in our base detector, but are discarded during final top-k selection because background receives higher scores. To mitigate this, we propose a class-agnostic ranker that estimates how well each predicted box fits an object and uses these scores to select the final predictions. Across three benchmarks, our detector improves unknown recall by 3.8% to 195.1% relative to the strongest baseline in each task, while maintaining competitive known-class detection. For categorizing, we draw on Euler diagrams, in which the region of a category contains the regions of its members. Our categorizer builds each category's region from the known classes and learns how much room to leave for members it has never seen. On the same detections, it categorizes unknown objects more accurately than existing hierarchical methods. Code is available at https://github.com/TUM-AVS/NEST.

**title/T1：** First-Hit Photoconsistency for Neural Surface Reconstruction

**abstract/A1：** Recent neural implicit and Gaussian splatting approaches have achieved impressive results in multi-view surface reconstruction. However, jointly optimizing geometry and appearance introduces ambiguities. A parametric appearance model can compensate for geometric errors, reproducing the input images accurately without an accurate surface. We demonstrate accurate neural implicit surface reconstruction using only multi-view patch photoconsistency with geometry-based visibility, without volumetric rendering or parametric appearance models. For each reference ray, sphere tracing computes the first surface intersection. Its position and normal define a local patch whose photoconsistency is evaluated across visible neighboring views using colors sampled directly from the input images. For efficient sphere tracing, we use a 1-Lipschitz multi-layer perceptron. We use a single photoconsistency loss, without foreground masks or auxiliary geometric regularization. Experiments show that our method achieves the lowest mean Chamfer distance on BlendedMVS (BMVS) among compared methods and matches the geometric accuracy of leading reconstruction methods on DTU.

These taxonomies contribute 2,228 dataset--category entries. RFW-R couples category-guided generation with collision geometry, composed physical properties, and interaction annotations; RFW-A uses reusable agent-authored procedural generators with explicit part and joint structure; RFW-S uses structure-aware simulation representations, calibration, and independent testing. A common interface preserves physical requirements specific to each asset type for retrieval and scene assembly. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that RFW-R provides broader asset coverage and stronger scene-fulfillment capabilities than existing datasets. Across five RoboTwin tasks, using 100 demonstrations per task for each asset source, policies trained on RFW-R achieve macro success rates of 71.2% in clean settings and 41.8% under randomization, exceeding the strongest baseline by 15.8 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively. RFW-W provides a scalable and unified asset foundation for generating physically grounded, task-conditioned embodied worlds.

**排除原因：** 该文研究超图信号在 t-谱域中的 score-based 扩散生成与缺失节点补全，属纯信号处理生成建模；其谱域前向过程与线性高斯引导依赖特定张量结构，与视觉推理中的 latent 状态、证据筛选或训练监督缺乏实质联系。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain

**abstract/A1：** We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes with the closed-form score elsewhere, which proves essential for stability at scale. A closed cosine-form observation operator turns missing-node recovery into linear-Gaussian guidance with stabilized posterior sampling. On hypergraphs of up to 500 nodes, our model beats a clique-expansion baseline by margins growing from $2\\times$ to $27\\times$ in covariance error, matches the graph-spectral statistics of the data better than the graph-basis model itself, and reaches the finite-sample estimation floor on data rotated off the t-spectral axes. Posterior sampling reduces missing-node NMSE to 0.28-0.64 (classical baselines 0.87-1.1) at conservative coverage, and cuts the framework's own denoising baseline by up to $3.6\\times$.

**abstract/A1：** Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise. Low-cost RGB cameras provide fine visible details to guide NIR reconstruction, but introduce spatially varying cross-camera misalignment. Supervised fusion methods require relatively large datasets of clean, high-resolution hyperspectral images, are sensitive to sensor noise, and generalize poorly across new sensors. We introduce SHARPnP, an interpretable, flexible framework coupling registration and reconstruction for RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy, unaligned measurements without clean references. We adapt a pretrained registration model via a cross-view loss backpropagated through a fixed plug-and-play fusion module. Temporal and recorrupted pairs enable reference-free self-supervision on noisy inputs. At test time, we calibrate cross-camera radiometry and refine alignment. Plug-and-play fusion employs sequential three-band denoising. On the REAL benchmark, SHARPnP outperforms supervised fusion baselines at $4\\times$, $8\\times$, and $16\\times$ on clean inputs and at $4\\times$ under Gaussian noise ($σ=5/255, 10/255$). On native RGB-HSI snapshot measurements, it reconstructs all 51 VIS-NIR bands, beyond the conventional 31-band VIS setting, without high-resolution references.

**排除原因：** 属于高光谱图像合成与底层视觉数据增广，未涉及 VLM 内部表征、latent 推理状态或证据获取与停止决策，缺乏与 LVR 研究主线的具体联系。
